comparison: Both address CNN classification results (C11-C14, C48, C61). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical testing and replication. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising serious concerns that poor within-scenario performance (60% accuracy) undermines conclusions about generalizability, stating the paper conflates whether CNNs can learn stability discrimination with whether learned representations generalize. This represents a fundamental disagreement about interpretation.

Both evaluate VTC multivoxel pattern analysis (C16-C18, C20, C47). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests, noting selective decoding for physical scenarios. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting these findings as part of the pattern showing lack of generalization in VTC, which contrasts with Physics Network and supports the main conclusion. Strong agreement.

Both address cross-scenario pattern correlation in Physics Network (C21-C23, C46). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, calling this 'critical evidence for abstract, scenario-invariant representations.' Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising a crucial concern that the key interaction (more generalization for stable-to-stable than stable-to-perilous) is not statistically tested, and that specificity is inferred from null effects in Animals-People rather than direct statistical comparison. Significant disagreement on adequacy of statistical evidence.

Both evaluate univariate Physics Network responses to stability (C35-C37, C40, C50, C67; OpenEval also includes C38-C39). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while acknowledging the evidence is 'preliminary.' Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising multiple concerns about alternative explanations: scene comprehension difficulty, implied motion, and likeliness-to-change rather than physical stability specifically. Reviewers state these alternatives must be 'ruled out conclusively' and 'simply acknowledging them will not be sufficient.' Disagreement on whether alternative explanations are adequately addressed.

Both address control analyses for confounds (C24-C29, C51). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while noting limitations (small eye tracking sample n=6, separate group for interestingness ratings). Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating interestingness ratings are 'not-quite-adequate' and suggesting distraction from another task would be better. Reviewers note lack of interaction in interestingness does not rule out scene comprehension confound. Disagreement on adequacy of control measures.

Both evaluate MT dissociation findings (C41-C45). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the finding strengthens the argument that Physics Network is not simply responding to predicted motion. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without specific concerns, though they questioned whether this successfully rules out alternative explanations in the context of univariate effects. General agreement.

Both address control region analyses (C32-C34). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting these demonstrate abstract stability representations are not widespread in visual cortex. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without major concerns, though noting some 'puzzling' patterns in Table 1 not discussed. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate anatomical specificity within Physics Network (C30-C31). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while cautioning about power limitations with n=13. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, treating these as supporting details without specific concerns. Agreement.

Both address the passive viewing/automatic extraction aspect (C59, C101). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED while noting participants were still attending for 1-back task. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED without concerns about this design feature. Agreement.

Both evaluate characterization of prior Physics Network literature (C53-C58; OpenEval also includes C95). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and important caveats about overlap with multiple demand system. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED after requesting deeper contextualization with prior work, particularly Schwettmann et al. (2019). Agreement after revision.

Both address the main theoretical conclusion about forward simulation (C52, C64, C68; peer review also includes C65-C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the conclusion is 'preliminary' and goes beyond what data definitively demonstrate, noting alternative mechanisms not fully ruled out. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns about all three lines of evidence and questioning the logic that unstable scenes require more simulation. Strong agreement that the simulation interpretation is not definitively established.

Both address speculative proposals about mechanisms and future directions (C69-C73). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting these are appropriately framed as hypotheses rather than tested claims. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting these as appropriate speculation without concerns. Minor difference in rating but agreement these are speculative rather than established.

OpenEval evaluates control analyses showing univariate stability effect is selective to Physics Network (C38-C39), rating SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these claims partially overlap with peer R4 which addresses broader univariate effects.
OpenEval evaluates characterization of prior CNN and theoretical work (C1-C3, C60), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates characterization of theoretical debate about rapid perception vs simulation (C5-C7, C63), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates stimulus screening procedure to control low-level visual confounds (C78-C80), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates validation of interestingness measure using IAPS (C81), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers questioned adequacy of interestingness ratings in R5.
OpenEval evaluates ROI definition procedure (C91-C92), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates successful ROI definition in all subjects (C15), rating SUPPORTED. No specific corresponding peer review evaluation found.
